- **20 overs per team**
- **6 legal balls per over**
- **10 wickets maximum**
- **First innings:** sets the target
- **Second innings:** chases the target
- **Toss:** choose to bat or field
- **Win:** finish with the higher score

- **Death:** 17–20

**Which batters perform best under high-pressure chase situations compared with low-pressure situations?**

Pressure depends on:

- **Required run rate**
- **Wickets in hand**
- **Balls remaining**

##### Does winning the toss and choosing to field (the more common decision in T20) actually translate into a meaningful advantage?

<div class="fragment">

Feature Engineering:

- Cleaned venue name inconsistencies across seasons.

- Binary Indicators:

  - `toss_winner_is_home_team`: did the toss winner enjoyed home-ground support?

  - `winner_same_as_toss_winner`: did the toss winner ultimately won the match?

- Converted venue and match condition variables into factors.

</div>

---

Baseline Win Rates by Toss Decision

<div style="font-size: 70%;">

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
coin_toss_advantage <- read_csv("Mark/coin_toss_advantage.csv" |> here::here())

# Summarize win rate by toss decision
toss_summary <- coin_toss_advantage |>
  group_by(toss_decision) |>
  summarise(
    total_matches = n(),
    toss_winner_wins = sum(winner_same_as_toss_winner, na.rm = TRUE),
    win_rate_pct = round(mean(winner_same_as_toss_winner, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 2)
  )
knitr::kable(toss_summary)
```

</div>

<br>

<div class="fragment">

Chi-Square Test of Independence

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Chi-Square Test of Independence
chisq.test(coin_toss_advantage$toss_decision,
           coin_toss_advantage$winner_same_as_toss_winner) |>
  broom::tidy() |>
  select(1:3) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  knitr::kable() |>
  kableExtra::column_spec(2, bold = TRUE)
```

- **Chi-Square Test Result:** winning the toss alone does not guarantee a competitive edge.

</div>

##### Does winning the toss and choosing to field (the more common decision in T20) actually translate into a meaningful advantage?

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
log_reg <- glm(
  winner_same_as_toss_winner ~ stadium + toss_decision + toss_winner_is_home_team,
  data = coin_toss_advantage,
  family = binomial
)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
sjPlot::tab_model(
  log_reg,
  show.intercept = FALSE,
  show.se = FALSE,
  show.r2 = TRUE,
  show.obs = TRUE,
  pred.labels = c(
    "Stadium",
    "Toss decision",
    "Home team won toss"
  ),
  dv.labels = "Same winner as toss winner",
  CSS = list(
    css.table = "font-size: 16px; width: 90%;",
    css.tdata = "padding: 5px;",
    css.thead = "font-size: 17px;",
    css.summary = "font-size: 14px;"
  )
)
```

---

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
sjPlot::tab_model(
  log_reg,
  terms = c("toss_decisionfield", "toss_winner_is_home_teamTRUE"),
  dv.labels = "Same winner as toss winner",
  show.aic = TRUE,
  show.loglik = TRUE
)
```

---

###### Key Findings & Insights

1. **Fielding First Effect:** The coefficient for choosing to field is statistically insignificant ($p > 0.05$).

2. **Home Advantage & Stadium Characteristics:** Home team advantage and venue-specific boundary dimensions hold far greater predictive power over match outcome than the coin toss.

3. **Strategic Takeaway:** Franchise teams over-index on the "chasing bias". Toss decisions should be tailored to pitch conditions and team composition rather than defaulting to fielding first.

##### Do players naturally cluster into distinct batting or bowling archetypes based on their ball-by-ball performance profiles?

::: {style="font-size: 60%;"}

| Feature Type | Batter Feature | Bowler Feature | Tactical Significance |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Efficiency** | `strike_rate` | `economy_rate` | Overall scoring pace vs. run restriction |
| **Control** | `dot_pct` | `dot_pct` | Strike rotation capability vs. pressure generation |
| **Aggression** | `boundary_pct` | `boundary_conceded_pct` | Big-hit frequency vs. boundary suppression |
| **Phase: PP** | `pp_ball_pct` | `pp_ball_pct` | Delivery volume in Overs 1–6 (Field Restrictions) |
| **Phase: Death** | `death_ball_pct` | `death_ball_pct` | Delivery volume in Overs 17–20 (High-Risk Finish) |

:::

::: {.fragment}
Apply k-means clustering
:::

---

##### Batters

::: {.fragment}

```{r, echo=FALSE,warning=FALSE,message=FALSE,out.width="100%"}
batter_stats <- read_csv("Mark/batter_stats.csv" |> here::here())

# Scale Features & Retain Player Names
batter_matrix <- batter_stats |>
  column_to_rownames("striker") |>
  select(-balls_faced) |>
  scale()

# Silhouette score with orginal data
factoextra::fviz_nbclust(batter_matrix, kmeans, method = "silhouette", nstart = 25) +
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 16),                       # General base font size
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),  # Plot title size
    axis.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold"),  # Axis label titles
    axis.text = element_text(size = 14)                   # Axis numbers (1, 2, 3...)
  )

# Run K-Means
km_res <- kmeans(batter_matrix, centers = 3, nstart = 25)

# Append cluster labels back to batter stats
batter_clustered <- batter_stats %>%
  mutate(cluster = as.factor(km_res$cluster))
```

:::

---

##### Batters

::: {.fragment}

```{r,echo=FALSE,warning=FALSE,message=FALSE,out.width="100%"}
# 1. Run PCA solely for 2D visual coordinates
pca_batter <- prcomp(batter_matrix)
pca_batter_df <- as.data.frame(pca_batter$x[, 1:2]) |>
  mutate(
    cluster = as.factor(km_res$cluster),
    player = rownames(batter_matrix)
  )

# 2. Plot PC1 vs PC2
ggplot(pca_batter_df, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = cluster)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  stat_ellipse(linetype = 2, alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "BBL Batter Archetypes",
    x = "PC1",
    y = "PC2",
    color = "Cluster"
  )
```

:::

---

##### Bowlers

::: {.fragment}

```{r,echo=FALSE,warning=FALSE,message=FALSE,out.width="100%"}
bowler_stats <- read_csv("Mark/bowler_stats.csv" |> here::here())

# Scale features for K-Means
bowler_matrix <- bowler_stats |>
  column_to_rownames("bowler") |>
  select(-balls_bowled) |>
  scale()

# Silhouette score with orginal data
factoextra::fviz_nbclust(bowler_matrix, kmeans, method = "silhouette", nstart = 25)

# Run K-Means
km_res <- kmeans(bowler_matrix, centers = 3, nstart = 25)

# Append cluster labels back to bowler stats
bowler_clustered <- bowler_stats %>%
  mutate(cluster = as.factor(km_res$cluster))
```

:::

---

##### Bowlers

::: {.fragment}

```{r,echo=FALSE,warning=FALSE,message=FALSE,out.width="100%"}
# 1. Run PCA solely for 2D visual coordinates
pca_bowler <- prcomp(bowler_matrix)
pca_bowler_df <- as.data.frame(pca_bowler$x[, 1:2]) |>
  mutate(
    cluster = as.factor(km_res$cluster),
    player = rownames(bowler_matrix)
  )

# 2. Plot PC1 vs PC2
ggplot(pca_bowler_df, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = cluster)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  stat_ellipse(linetype = 2, alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "BBL Bowler Archetypes",
    x = "PC1",
```
